intended_object: The natural inclusion of the finite part of the closed upper half-plane ℍ ∪ ∂ℍ (with ∂ℍ = ℝ ∪ {∞}) into ℂ: a point z ∈ ℍ goes to z, a real boundary point x goes to x. The value at ∞ is left as junk. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Walkden §7.1).
explanation: The library models ℍ ∪ ∂ℍ as `ℍ ⊕ OnePoint ℝ`. On `Sum.inl z` the definition gives the coercion `(z : ℂ)`. On `Sum.inr ξ` it gives `OnePoint.elim ξ 0 id`, cast to ℂ. In Mathlib, `OnePoint.elim : OnePoint X → Y → (X → Y) → Y` sends ∞ to the default value (here 0) and a point `↑x` to `id x = x`. So a real boundary point x goes to `(x : ℂ)` and ∞ goes to 0. The docstring says the value 0 at ∞ is junk with no meaning, so this follows the usual junk-value convention. On ℍ ∪ ℝ the map is the standard embedding into ℂ: it is injective there, and its image is the closed upper half-plane {Im ≥ 0}. The lemmas `im_toComplex_nonneg` and `toComplex_injOn` confirm this. The construction is specific to the upper half-plane, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no definition of this map on `ℍ ⊕ OnePoint ℝ`.
